quiz.title: Module 1 — The Foundations of Video Editing
quiz.description: Monday's quiz covers what video editing is, the role of the editor, understanding your footage, aspect ratio, frame rate and resolution, and finding your way around the CapCut Mobile workspace.

questions.prompt: What is one of the main purposes of video editing?
options: To increase the file size of a video
To transform raw footage into a coherent finished video
To record footage directly from a camera
To increase the frame rate of every video
questions.explanation: Editing takes the raw footage you shot and shapes it into something coherent — a finished video with a clear structure and meaning.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the role of a video editor?
options: Simply combining every piece of footage that was recorded
Only adding visual effects and transitions
Selecting, arranging, and manipulating footage to shape the viewer's experience
Recording all the footage used in a project
questions.explanation: An editor is not a passive assembler. You select what matters, arrange it, and manipulate it so the viewer feels and understands what you intend.

questions.prompt: Why is it important for an editor to understand their footage before beginning an edit?
options: It allows the editor to identify useful material and understand what they are working with
It automatically improves the resolution of the footage
It eliminates the need to arrange clips
It prevents the video from needing audio
questions.explanation: Watching and reviewing your footage first tells you what you actually have, so you can decide what is worth using and what the material needs.

questions.prompt: What does the aspect ratio of a video describe?
options: How loud the video's audio is
The number of frames displayed every second
The relationship between the width and height of the video frame
The amount of storage space required by the video
questions.explanation: Aspect ratio is the width-to-height relationship of the frame — for example 16:9 landscape or 9:16 portrait.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes frame rate from resolution?
options: Frame rate describes image dimensions, while resolution describes audio quality
Frame rate describes how many frames are displayed per second, while resolution describes the image's dimensions/detail
Frame rate and resolution are two different names for the same thing
Resolution determines how many frames are displayed per second
questions.explanation: Frame rate is about motion — how many frames pass each second. Resolution is about detail — the dimensions of the image.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of becoming familiar with the CapCut Mobile interface before beginning actual editing?
options: To memorize every effect in the application
To make the editing environment and its major tools easier to navigate
To increase the storage capacity of the phone
To automatically complete future editing projects
questions.explanation: Knowing where the major tools live means you spend your time editing rather than hunting for buttons.

questions.prompt: Which of the following can be imported into a CapCut project as an asset?
options: Only video clips
Only photographs
Only music files
Video clips, images, audio, music, and other media
questions.explanation: A project can hold many kinds of media — video, images, audio, music and more — not just one type.

questions.prompt: A beginner opens CapCut and immediately starts adding transitions and effects without first understanding the footage or the editing workspace. What is the biggest problem with this approach?
options: Transitions cannot be used in CapCut Mobile
Effects automatically reduce every video's resolution
The editor may be manipulating footage without understanding what the material requires or how the editing environment works
CapCut only allows effects to be added after exporting the video
questions.explanation: Effects are not a substitute for understanding. Without knowing your footage or your workspace, you are adding decoration rather than making editing decisions.
